author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Calibrate analog-stick dead zones for PS2 games
summary: Measure neutral drift and full circular travel, raise the inner dead zone only above observed noise, verify fine movement and maximum range in two game contexts, then repeat after controller reconnect.
heroAlt: LilyPad controller settings exposing sensitivity and dead-zone calibration controls

sourceLabels.android-game-controller: Android controller events, axes, and device behavior

blocks.text: Measure idle noise before adding a dead zone

An inner dead zone should cover the controller's real neutral noise without erasing small steering or camera adjustments. Place the controller on a stable surface, observe each stick for at least thirty seconds, and note the largest unintended value. Move in slow circles to reveal asymmetry and confirm the outer range. Calibrate one stick at a time and keep any title-specific sensitivity separate.
Do not use a large dead zone to hide severe or rapidly worsening hardware drift. It can make precise movement impossible and delay a necessary controller repair.

items: Controller fully charged or connected through stable USB.
A live axis display with numeric or clear visual position.
Default sensitivity, curve, and dead-zone values recorded.
One aiming or camera scene and one steering or movement scene.
Controller resting untouched before every neutral sample.

blocks.text: Set the smallest stable inner boundary

items: 1. Observe the left stick untouched and record maximum neutral deviation on both axes.
2. Repeat the observation for the right stick.
3. Increase the affected inner dead zone just beyond consistent noise, one small step at a time.
4. Move slowly from center and confirm response begins smoothly in every direction.
5. Trace full circles and verify cardinal plus diagonal maximum range.
6. Test fine aiming or camera movement in the first game scene.
7. Test sustained steering or walking in the second scene.
8. Reconnect the controller and repeat neutral plus full-range checks.

blocks.text: Neutral measurement creates an evidence-based lower bound. Slow movement tests reveal a dead zone that is technically stable but too large for control. Circular travel exposes axis clipping, square gates, and asymmetric hardware that a four-direction test can miss.
The chosen value must stop idle movement while preserving deliberate small and full-scale input.

items: Both sticks remain neutral while untouched.
Fine motion begins without a large jump.
All cardinal and diagonal directions reach expected range.
Aiming and steering remain controllable.
Reconnect does not reintroduce drift or change the profile.

blocks.text: Calibration results that point to hardware

items: Neutral values wander beyond the new boundary: clean or repair the stick.
One direction never reaches full range: inspect outer calibration or hardware wear.
Only Bluetooth shows spikes: compare a wired path.
One title feels wrong with a good tester result: use a per-game sensitivity profile.

blocks.text: Restore the original dead-zone, sensitivity, and curve values, reload the previous controller profile, and confirm the unaffected stick still behaves normally. Mark the drifting device rather than applying its correction globally.
Inner dead zone and response curve solve different problems

The dead zone suppresses small neutral noise; a response curve changes how deliberate travel maps across the range. Adjusting both together makes it difficult to know which change harmed precision. Measure each stick independently because worn potentiometers can drift asymmetrically and a value suitable for the left stick may make the camera stick feel blunt. Recheck after reconnect and after the controller warms in use; rapidly growing neutral error is a hardware warning, not a reason to keep expanding the software dead zone.
